prisoner.name: Rev. Bill Hogan
prisoner.description: Rev. Bill Hogan was jailed following an anti-nuclear protest at the LaSalle nuclear power plant in Illinois. A contemporary June 1983 report records an April 20 trespass conviction and a thirty-day contempt sentence after the two defendants spoke about the dangers of nuclear power despite the judge's order. An additional fifteen-day trespass sentence followed. Both were released on appeal bond on May 23, 1983.
prisoner.body: Source: Nuclear Resister 17, June 6, 1983, page 4. The reported thirty- and fifteen-day sentences are not stored as actual time served.

case.charges: Trespass at LaSalle nuclear power plant; contempt of court for speaking about nuclear power during closing statements.
case.convicted: Trespass conviction April 20, 1983; contempt also reported.
case.sentence: Thirty days for contempt and an additional fifteen days for trespass; released on appeal bond May 23, 1983. Custody began in April 1983; the exact admission day and actual total served remain unverified. The protest occurred in June 1982; exact initial arrest date unverified.
